sundar.14.cau1: Recognising him as a devotee of Hari, Sītā felt a deep and intense love; tears came to her eyes, and the hair on her body stood on end. Hanumān, dear one, I was drowning in the ocean of separation, and you have become a ship for me.
sundar.14.cau2: Now tell me, and may I be a sacrifice for you, how Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara and home of joy, fares with his younger brother. Śrī Rāma is tender-hearted and compassionate; why, Hanumān, has he put on such hardness?
sundar.14.cau3: Does Śrī Rāma, whose very nature it is to give joy to his servants, ever think of me? Dear one, will my eyes ever be cooled by gazing on his dark and tender form?
sundar.14.cau4: No words would come, and her eyes filled with tears: Alas, my Lord, you have forgotten me utterly! Seeing Sītā so overwhelmed by the pain of separation, Hanumān spoke to her gently and humbly.
sundar.14.cau5: Mother, the Lord is well, and his younger brother with him; but he, the abode of grace, grieves at your grief. Mother, do not be downcast at heart: Śrī Rāma's love is twice as great as yours.
sundar.14.do14: Mother, take heart now and listen to Śrī Rāma's message. Saying this, Hanumān was overcome, his voice faltering and his eyes brimming with tears.
sundar.15.cau1: Śrī Rāma said: Sītā, in separation from you, all things have turned contrary for me. The trees' new leaves seem like fire, night is like the night of doom, and the moon like the sun.
sundar.15.cau2: Beds of blue lotuses seem a forest of spears, and the clouds seem to rain boiling oil. Things that once did me good now give me pain, and the breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, is like a serpent's breath.
sundar.15.cau3: Grief grows a little lighter even by being told, but whom shall I tell? No one understands it. Beloved, the truth of the love between you and me is known to my mind alone.
sundar.15.cau4: And that mind stays always with you; from this much alone, know the essence of my love. Hearing the Lord's message, Sītā was so immersed in love that she was no longer aware of her body.
sundar.15.cau5: Hanumān said: Mother, take heart, and remember Śrī Rāma, who gives joy to his servants. Call to mind the majesty of Śrī Rāma, and hearing my words, give up your faint-heartedness.
sundar.15.do15: The demon hordes are like moths, and Śrī Rāma's arrows like fire. Mother, take heart: think of the demons as already burnt.
sundar.16.cau1: Had Śrī Rāma received news of you, he would have made no delay. Jānakī, once the sun of Śrī Rāma's arrows rises, where will the darkness of the demon hosts be?
sundar.16.cau2: Mother, I would take you with me right now; but the Lord has not commanded it, I swear by Śrī Rāma. Mother, be patient a few days more; Śrī Rāma will come with the monkeys.
sundar.16.cau3: He will slay the demons and take you away, and Nārada and others will sing his fame in all three worlds. Son, the monkeys are all like you, and the demons are very mighty warriors.
sundar.16.cau4: There is great doubt in my heart. Hearing this, Hanumān revealed his own true body, vast as a golden mountain, fearsome in battle: a hero of immense strength.
sundar.16.cau5: Then trust came into Sītā's mind, and Hanumān, son of the Wind, again took on a small form.
sundar.16.do16: Listen, Mother: a monkey has no great strength or wisdom; yet by the Lord's might even the tiniest snake can eat up Garuḍa.
sundar.17.cau1: Sītā's heart was content as she heard Hanumān's words, steeped in devotion, glory, splendour and strength. Knowing him to be dear to Śrī Rāma, she blessed him: Dear one, may you be a treasury of strength and good character.
sundar.17.cau2: Son, may you be free from age and death and a treasury of virtues, and may Śrī Rāma show you great affection. Hearing with his own ears the wish that the Lord might be gracious to him, Hanumān was utterly immersed in love.
sundar.17.cau3: Time after time Hanumān laid his head at her feet; then, folding his hands, he said: Mother, now I have achieved all I could wish for; your blessing is famed as one that never fails.
sundar.17.cau4: Listen, Mother: seeing the lovely fruit on these trees, I feel very hungry. Listen, son: those who keep watch over the grove are demons, great and mighty warriors.
sundar.17.cau5: Mother, I have no fear of them, if it pleases you at heart.
sundar.17.do17: Seeing that Hanumān was skilled in intelligence and in strength, Sītā said: Go, dear one; keep Śrī Rāma's feet in your heart and eat the sweet fruit.
sundar.18.cau1: He bowed his head, set off and entered the garden. He ate the fruit and began to break the trees. Many warriors stood guard there; some he killed, and some went off and raised the alarm.
sundar.18.cau2: My lord, a huge monkey has come and ravaged the Aśoka grove. He has been eating the fruit and tearing up the trees, and he has crushed the guards one after another and thrown them to the ground.
sundar.18.cau3: Hearing this, Rāvaṇa sent many warriors. At the sight of them Hanumān roared. He slew all the demons; a few, left half-dead, ran off crying out.
sundar.18.cau4: Then Rāvaṇa sent Akṣaya Kumāra, who set out with countless fine warriors. Seeing him approach, Hanumān grasped a tree and challenged him; he felled him and let out a mighty roar.
sundar.18.do18: Some he killed, some he crushed, some he caught and mixed with the dust; and some once more went and cried: My lord, the monkey's strength is enormous.
sundar.19.cau1: Hearing that his son had been slain, Rāvaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, was enraged and sent the mighty Meghanāda: Do not kill him, my son; bind him. Let us see this monkey and where he comes from.
sundar.19.cau2: Indrajit, the matchless warrior, set out, anger welling up in him when he heard his brother had been killed. Hanumān saw that a fearsome warrior had come; gnashing his teeth, he roared and rushed at him.
sundar.19.cau3: He uprooted an enormous tree and left the son of the lord of Laṅkā without a chariot. The great warriors who were with him Hanumān seized one after another and crushed against his own body.
sundar.19.cau4: Having felled them, he closed with Meghanāda, and the two fought like a pair of mighty elephants. Hanumān struck him with his fist and went and climbed a tree; for a moment Meghanāda lay senseless.
sundar.19.cau5: Getting up again, he wove many illusions, yet the son of the Wind could not be defeated.
sundar.19.do19: He aimed the weapon of Brahmā, and Hanumān thought to himself: If I do not honour Brahmā's arrow, its boundless glory will be lost.
sundar.20.cau1: He struck Hanumān with Brahmā's arrow; even in falling, Hanumān destroyed the host. Seeing Hanumān fall senseless, Meghanāda bound him with a serpent noose and took him away.
sundar.20.cau2: Listen, Pārvatī: by repeating his name the wise cut the bonds of worldly existence; could his messenger ever fall into bonds? It was for the Lord's work that Hanumān let himself be bound.
sundar.20.cau3: Hearing that Hanumān had been bound, the demons came running, and all of them gathered in the court to see the spectacle. Hanumān came there and saw Rāvaṇa's court; its grandeur was beyond words.
sundar.20.cau4: Gods and the guardians of the quarters stood humbly with joined palms, all of them watching his brow in fear. Seeing such power, Hanumān felt no fear at all, as Garuḍa is fearless in the midst of a host of serpents.
sundar.20.do20: Looking at Hanumān, Rāvaṇa laughed, uttering words of abuse; then he remembered his son's death, and grief rose in his heart.
sundar.21.cau1: Rāvaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: Monkey, who are you? On whose strength did you lay waste the grove? Or is it that you have never heard of me? I see you are utterly without fear, you wretch.
sundar.21.cau2: What offence did the demons commit, that you killed them? Tell me, wretch, have you no care for your life? Hear me, Rāvaṇa: he whose strength enables māyā to fashion the hosts of universes;
sundar.21.cau3: through whose strength, ten-headed one, Brahmā creates, Hari preserves and Śiva dissolves; through whose strength the thousand-faced Śeṣa holds up on his head the universe itself, its mountains and forests too;
sundar.21.cau4: who, as protector of the gods, takes bodies of many kinds, and who teaches wretches like you a lesson; who broke the unyielding bow of Śiva and with it crushed the pride of the assembled kings;
sundar.21.cau5: who slew Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśirā and Vālī, every one of them a warrior of matchless strength;
sundar.21.do21: by the merest fraction of whose strength you conquered all creation, moving and unmoving: I am the messenger of him whose beloved wife you have carried off and brought here.
